key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects, making PEA2PbI4 more resistant to ambient light and thermal degradation than BA2PbI4.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve two-dimensional perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskite nanoflakes.
Assessed ambient photo- and thermal stability using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Probed chemical degradation using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite sharing organic-component loss and decomposition into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or operational lifetime, so device-level benefits remain unverified.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
